extracted.intended_audience: members of Congress, regulators (EPA/CARB), Volkswagen executives/staff, dealers, affected consumers, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Transcript of a congressional oversight hearing questioning Volkswagen leadership about the emissions 'defeat device', remediation, testing, corporate responsibility, and consumer restitution. Contains expectations and standards articulated by lawmakers for acceptable company conduct and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify affected owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected owners should be personally notified; many owners have received no letter and cannot determine from the vehicle/manual whether they are affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members noted they "have received no letter" and encouraged using tools (VIN lookup) so owners who "are not capable of taking apart the engine and figuring out if they are an EA 189" can learn if they are affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify affected vehicle generation (Generation 1 vs Generation 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish whether a vehicle is Generation 1 or Generation 2 and make that information accessible to owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawmakers suggested a "pretty simple website that takes the VIN numbers that are affected and says you are Generation 1, you are Generation 2," noting the fix for Generation 2 "is more simple than for 1."

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore trust by standing behind vehicles / buyback program
rubrics_metrics.description: Company should offer to buy back affected cars at pre-notice fair market value to restore consumer trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative advice: "one of the ways to do that is to stand behind your vehicle... buy these cars back... buy your car back at what the fair market value of that vehicle was prior to this notice coming out." Example given of prior no-questions-asked dealer service as a trust-building precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make consumers whole for lost performance and resale value
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies must consider that fixes to comply with emissions may reduce performance and have destroyed resale value; consumers were defrauded and deserve appropriate compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members stated consumers "have every right to feel defrauded" and warned "whatever fixes to comply with emissions standards will hurt the vehicles' performance in other ways" and that "the resell value... has certainly been destroyed."

rubrics_metrics.name: Set aside adequate funds and provide honest financial disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Company should accurately estimate and reserve sufficient funds to cover remediation, buybacks, and settlements — current estimates may be orders of magnitude too low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative Collins: "Six point five billion euros is off by an order of magnitude... I would suggest you start doing that tomorrow... I would suggest you are off by an order of magnitude."

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not shift settlement costs to taxpayers (avoid tax loopholes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Company should commit not to use tax code loopholes to shift the burden of settlement costs to taxpayers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members referenced BP's settlement that allowed tax-shifting and asked VW to "commit here today under oath that VW will not use this loophole to write off any future settlement payments related to the fraudulent and deceptive activity."

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct thorough internal investigations to determine who knew and why
rubrics_metrics.description: Company must investigate and report who made the decisions, how the deception happened, and whether it extended beyond a few individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawmakers demanded investigations to "find out what drove those people" and to examine whether the misconduct "goes way, way higher than that" rather than blaming just "a couple of rogue engineers."

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose timelines and communications about when company became aware
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear answers and records about when VW first learned of independent research and what actions were taken and when.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions asked: "When did VW first become aware of this research?" (answer given: "The end of April... Mid-May I got information"), and members requested records of presentations/discussions with EPA/CARB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retest and validate external research using company equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Company engineering departments should recheck independent testing results on their own equipment to validate findings before responding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Horn described steps: (1) acknowledge emission violations, (2) engineering departments "recheck those testing results on our own equipment in order to validate this," and (3) implement corrective software actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate and cooperate with regulators and foreign authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Work closely with EPA, CARB, the German KBA, and other agencies; provide records of interactions and cooperate with investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcript references: "working with those agencies; also, with the German KBA" and requests for who within VW interacted with EPA and CARB and whether they were VW America or VW AG personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use real-world road testing (not solely dyno testing) to detect discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing regimes must include independent road tests in addition to dyno tests to detect on-road emissions discrepancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Horn acknowledged that engineers "tested the dyno situation for the cars and they didn't do independent road tests," which was cited as a gap in detecting the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure transparency and collaboration among testing/compliance offices (Oxnard, Auburn Hills)
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing and certification facilities and application/compliance offices should collaborate, be transparent, and share data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about the role of Oxnard (testing) and Auburn Hills (applications/certification) and whether they worked together; member noted facilities are now "under one roof" and pressed for clarity on collaboration and roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature attribution to 'rogue engineers' without evidence — examine corporate culture and pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept a narrative that misconduct was limited to a few individuals without investigating corporate incentives, cost pressure, and managerial decisions that may have enabled it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple members rejected VW's 'rogue engineers' explanation, urging examination of patent processes, engineering management, and corporate profit/pressure dynamics that could have driven the conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and mitigate economic impact on dealers and employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize dealers will bear expenses (lost sales) and ensure remedies account for dealer and employee impacts; dealers should not be left to absorb costs alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members said VW dealers "care about their customers" but "this is going to be an expense to them because they are not selling cars that are bringing in profits" and dealers "will stand by their employees" but need support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear, truthful answers under oath and be prepared to explain tax/legal positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Executives should be able to give clear commitments under oath (e.g., tax-treatment of settlements) or explain constraints if they cannot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asked for a "clear answer under oath" about tax loophole use, Mr. Horn replied he would need to understand tax details; members pressed for explicit commitments not to shift burdens to taxpayers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review patent/IP processes when novel technical solutions appear
rubrics_metrics.description: If a purported technical solution yields a breakthrough, it should have been reviewed by IP/patent departments; failure to do so suggests deeper organizational problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative Collins argued that if the software was a true breakthrough it would have been patented and that failure to escalate suggests either incompetence or complicity: "Why didn't we look for patents? ... Patent Department should be terminated."
